$comment: EXPERIMENTAL — declarative mapping from the canonical Part III instance-data model (criterion C01, exg-crim-part) to UBL QualificationApplicationResponse XML. The real ESPD-EDM UBL emits (a) one cac:TenderingCriterion declaration, (b) a FLAT list of cac:TenderingCriterionResponse elements each keyed to the answered property via cac:ValidatedCriterionPropertyID/cbc:ID, and (c) a separate cac:Evidence list linked from a response by cac:EvidenceSupplied/cbc:ID. All of this is expressed with the ENGINE-GENERIC `records` construct: the engine hardcodes no UBL element names — every element path (the record wrapper, its key element, its scheme attribute, the value/period/reference targets) is supplied here in the spec.

$notes.records: A `records` rule emits a repeated 'record' wrapper element, each carrying a `key` (an identifier element, optionally with a scheme attribute) and a `body` that is exactly ONE of: a typed `value`, a `period`, or `references` (repeated cross-reference elements). This is generic: for ESPD responses the wrapper is cac:TenderingCriterionResponse, the key is cac:ValidatedCriterionPropertyID/cbc:ID (schemeID='criterion'), and the bodies map to cac:ResponseValue/* , cac:ApplicablePeriod, cac:EvidenceSupplied. Nothing about those names is in the engine. `entries` gives a fixed set of records; `forEach` expands one entries-set per instance-array item (records then share key ids, distinguished by document order on import — see repeatKeys).
$notes.valueAttributes: A `value` body may carry `attributes`, using the same convention as the base value rule: a constant (e.g. { "unitCode": "YEAR" } for QUANTITY_YEAR, fixed by the question) or a data-sourced reference (e.g. { "currencyID": { "from": "currency" } } for AMOUNT, entered by the EO). Constant attributes are discriminators only; data-sourced attributes roundtrip back into the instance data. This covers BR-TCR-08 numeric datatypes (AMOUNT->cbc:ResponseAmount@currencyID, QUANTITY*->cbc:ResponseQuantity@unitCode) needed by the selection criteria.
$notes.propertyKey: The record key identifies the answered property (Schematron BR-TCR-01-01/-01-02). The EA export carries the `requestpath` (e.g. C01_exg-crim-part/QG1/Q1), the authentic 'XML Path like ID' the Schematron supports and the .rif scripts use with schemeID='criterion'. Emitted as-is rather than fabricating v5 UUIDs; when UUIDs are available upstream only the per-entry `key` strings change.
$notes.repeatKeys: Repeated conviction records (QSG1, 0..n) share the SAME key id deliberately (Schematron disabled uniqueness rule BR-TCR-01-03 for XML-path ids). Occurrence order is carried by document order of the repeated records; import groups them into array items in order.
$notes.datatypes: The value target is dictated by the property's ValueDataTypeCode (BR-TCR-08): INDICATOR -> cac:ResponseValue/cbc:ResponseIndicator; DESCRIPTION -> cac:ResponseValue/cbc:Description; DATE -> cac:ResponseValue/cbc:ResponseDate; PERIOD -> cac:ApplicablePeriod (own branch, BR-TCR-08-09).
$notes.evidence: Per BR-TCR-03 each record body is exactly one branch, so QG2/Q1 (INDICATOR value) and QG2/QSG1/Q1 (EVIDENCE_IDENTIFIER references) are separate records. The link is explicit and declarative: evidence[].id (producer-owned) is mapped to the cac:Evidence key element, and the QG2/QSG1/Q1 record's `references` emits one cac:EvidenceSupplied/cbc:ID per evidence entry valued by the same `key` field (BR-TCR-09). The engine invents no ids; fully bidirectional.
$notes.period: exclusionPeriod maps structured startDate/endDate to cac:ApplicablePeriod. A description-only period has no ApplicablePeriod home (StartDate/EndDate/DurationMeasure only) — documented gap.

rules.$comment: C01 criterion declaration — criterion UUID (from the EA export). Pure constant metadata: no instance-data home, not written back on import.
Non-repeating answer records. Each `entries` item emits one record wrapper (cac:TenderingCriterionResponse) with a keyed property id and one body branch.

entries.$comment: QG2/QSG1/Q1 — 'Evidence Supplied' (EVIDENCE_IDENTIFIER, 1..n). Body is `references`: one cac:EvidenceSupplied/cbc:ID per evidence entry, valued by that entry's `key` field (producer-owned id). Links to the cac:Evidence records below (BR-TCR-09).

rules.$comment: Repeating conviction records (C01/QG1/QSG1, 0..n). `forEach` expands the entries-set once per conviction; entry sources resolve against the array item. Repeated records share their key ids; occurrence order = document order.

entries.$comment: PERIOD (BR-TCR-08-09) — cac:ApplicablePeriod branch, not a ResponseValue child.

rules.$comment: Evidence documents (cac:Evidence, 1..n). A `records` rule with `forEach` + `item.fields`: one record per evidence entry, all fields inside it. The entity id (rule `key`) is just the field mapped to the key element — the engine generates no ids; the QG2/QSG1/Q1 record above references these same ids.
